label: D2 after choosing a1 and reaching S1 (common), following a rewarded trial, mid-episode
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a1 and the state input shows S1 (a common a1->S1 transition). It almost never fires on S2, on rare transitions, or at D1/GO. Within that, it mostly needs the previous trial to have been rewarded (the D1 reward input of the same trial): prev_reward==1 takes F1 from 0.61 to 0.73. It is also strongly gated by time in the episode: low over trials 0-19, peaks around trials 50-70, and is nearly silent after trial 80. Adding the 20<=ep_trial<80 window raises dev F1 to 0.82 (P 0.83, R 0.81, mass recall 0.86). All variables are observed at D2 (action and state are shown then), so no future variables are used. Magnitude: the largest activations (about 1.0) come on the first a1->S1 common trial after a run of a2 choices (often a2 trials that reached S1 by a rare transition and were rewarded), i.e. switching to a1 and landing in S1. During long a1->S1c streaks it fires weakly (0.05-0.3) and grows slowly from trial to trial. Activation is higher when the model value is high (top value bin: 48% of mass). The episode-time dependence suggests a slow drift in the hidden state, not a task variable.

issues: Reproduced the scores. Test: P 0.833, R 0.803, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.864. Dev: F1 0.820. All D1 and GO activations are exactly 0, so 'almost never fires at D1/GO' understates it: the feature fires only at D2.

Checked the S1 / common / a1 claim. Every active step is at state S1 (state==2 never fires). action==2 (a2 reaching S1 by a rare transition) is active on only 444 of 56858 steps and gets 0.1% of the mass, at tiny activations (about 0.05).

Checked the build-up of F1. D2&a1&S1 alone: F1 0.605. Adding prev_reward==1: 0.732. Adding the 20<=ep_trial<80 window: 0.820. These match the claims. With prev_reward==0 the precision is only 0.097. At ep_trial>=80 the precision is 0.048 and the activation rate is 0.010 at trials 80-89 and 0.000 at 90-99. Below trial 20 the precision is 0.24. So the time gating is real.

Minor refinement: the previous reward mostly needs to have come from S1 (the top windows are a2->S1 rare and rewarded, then a1->S1 common). Within the predicate, prev_state==2 gives P 0.49 but covers only 2.9% of activations. Adding prev_state!=2 gives F1 0.815 vs 0.820, so it makes no material difference.

The remaining false positives are systematic but graded: a1->S1 common rewarded trials shortly after an unrewarded or S2-rare trial inside an a1 streak, where the activation is still near zero. Example: when tv('reward',-2)==0 inside the predicate, P drops to 0.61. Excluding that class raises P to 0.877 but lowers F1 to 0.804. This matches the explanation's 'grows slowly from trial to trial' during a1->S1c streaks rather than refuting it.
The good state is a weak extra factor: requiring good==1 lowers F1 to 0.688, so the label is right not to use it.
The missed activations (13.6% of the mass) are mostly weak a1->S1c steps outside the 20-80 time window or just after an unrewarded trial. They are not a separate class of firing.
